$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs the same steps locally.
`status` is `oracle-backed` (CI regenerates the golden in the pinned container and compares
it on every run) or `unchecked` (the golden is committed and read by the Rust tests, but no
CI step has ever re-derived it). The distinction is part of the claim each suite supports.
Jobs that are analysis rather than comparison stay hand-written in ci.template.yml: the
jmath corpus diff and the pow probe of decision 0007, and the JVM number-format sweep of
decision 0017, which asserts measured rates rather than byte equality.

ci.$why: Suites are grouped into jobs of this size: one job per suite would restore the oracle image once per suite, and one job for all of them is what the hand-written workflow did, where a failing suite hid every suite after it.

suites.title: The BED codec
suites.why: BEDCodec is what GATK's -L regions.bed runs through, so its coordinate convention is the one a whole interval argument inherits, and five of its decisions are not what a BED parser suggests. The start is shifted by a constructor argument, StartOffset.ONE being the default, so a file's 0-based start becomes 1-based on the way in and the feature carries the shifted number without carrying the shift. A two-token line is a point rather than a zero-length interval, because with no end column the end is the shifted start: one base at a coordinate the file never mentions. The separator is the regex tab-or-a-run-of-spaces with limit -1, so a run of spaces however long is one separator, a tab beside a space is two, and a trailing separator produces an empty field rather than being dropped. A blank line and a header line decode to null rather than to an error, and the header prefixes are matched on the raw line so a leading space makes them data. And a score that does not parse returns the feature early, so a line whose score is a dot keeps its name and silently loses its strand, its colour and its exons even though those columns are present and well formed, while every other malformed number in the same line throws instead.

suites.title: The IntervalList codec
suites.why: IntervalListCodec is what GATK's -L regions.interval_list runs through, and it is a stricter parser than the reader htsjdk uses on the same file, so whether an interval list is valid depends on which door it came through. The field count is checked against five exactly and is counted after String.split has dropped trailing empty fields, so a line ending in a tab is refused for its count rather than for its empty name. The strand column is decoded by Strand.decode, which answers NONE for anything that is not a single plus or minus, and NONE is then rejected, so a dot is a legal strand in the BED codec of the same package and an error here. An interval on a contig the dictionary does not hold is dropped with a warning and the file still loads, while an interval past the end of a contig it does hold fails the whole read, and that length check is switched off by a declared length of zero. And start equal to end plus one is a legal empty interval while start equal to end plus two is refused with a message quoting a film, which is observable output and therefore part of the port.

suites.title: VCFCodec.canDecode, the codec that opens the file
suites.why: VCFCodec is the third codec GATK's -L reaches and the only one that decides by content rather than by path. BEDCodec and IntervalListCodec answer canDecode on the extension, so a .list holding a BED body is not a Feature file and dies in the interval reader; a .list holding a VCF body is one, because this codec reads the first eighteen bytes and finds the magic. Two files with the same extension and different contents therefore take different branches of -L, and only this codec makes that true. It tries plain, then GZIPInputStream, then BlockCompressedInputStream, and since a BGZF file is a gzip file the second attempt already answers for the third. The read's return value is computed and never used, so a file shorter than the magic leaves zero bytes in the tail of the buffer and answers false rather than throwing, and an absent path answers false through a caught IOException. The magic carries no minor version, so 4.0 through 4.3 all match and 3.3 does not; VCF3Codec carries the other magic and GATK registers both.

suites.title: BGZF blocks
suites.why: The committed goldens were produced under Rosetta on Apple Silicon. If real silicon disagrees, every claim resting on them is void, so this must fail loudly.

compare.why: The corpus is a literal array in the Rust test rather than a .txt.gz, so both sides are read with the same pattern; only the shared cases are compared, since the test carries cases the dump does not emit.

suites.title: BAM record codec
suites.why: The BAM record codec is pure integer work, so unlike the math corpus there is no reason to expect emulation to change it. That is the hypothesis; this measures it, because "no reason to expect" is how decision 0004's wrong assumption got in.

suites.title: BAM file and header
suites.why: These carry compressed bytes, so unlike the record codec they do depend on the deflate implementation. Decision 0001 pins it; this is what would catch that pin coming loose.

suites.title: BAM reheader
suites.why: The reheadered BAM is block-copied, so it carries compressed bytes and depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001), exactly like the BAM file goldens. Comment rows share a (kind, case) key so only the last per case is diffed here, but the reheadered hex encodes every comment in its header, so any comment drift shows up there.

suites.title: BAM gather
suites.why: The gathered BAM is block-copied, so it carries compressed bytes and depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001). Input rows share a (kind, case) key so only the last per case is diffed here, but the gathered hex is the concatenation of them all.

suites.title: BuildBamIndex (read-side BAI)
suites.why: The read-side .bai carries compressed-stream virtual offsets, so it depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001) exactly like the BAM goldens, and it differs from the write-side BAI.

suites.title: Interval lists
suites.why: Some cases have an empty value: an empty interval list is a result, not a missing row, so valueless lines are kept rather than skipped.

suites.title: Reading a VCF header
suites.why: Everything else here writes VCF; nothing reads one, and GATK's VariantWalker cannot exist without a reader. Two layers are measured. VCFHeaderLineTranslator's VCF4Parser is a hand-written scanner whose switch falls through from the '<' case into the '>' case, so an unquoted '<' away from position 0 is dropped, an unquoted '>' anywhere is dropped, and a line that does not end in '>' loses its last field entirely and silently: a port written from the VCF specification would keep those characters and store that field. Quotes are a toggle rather than a delimiter, because the quote test precedes the in-quote test, so a quote in the middle of an unquoted value opens a quoted region and the comma after it stops separating fields; inside a quote a backslash before anything but a quote or a backslash is kept together with the character. VCFCodec.readActualHeader is the second layer: it splits the version line on every '=' and records a version only when that yields exactly two fields, so a line with an extra '=' records nothing and fails later with a different message. The refusals carry their messages because the messages separate two failures of the same file. Only unstructured meta lines are fed to the frame; turning an INFO line into a typed compound header line is the next layer and is measured on its own, since mixing them would leave a failure ambiguous between the two.

suites.title: One ## line into a typed header line
suites.why: The scanner suite says which pairs a line carries; this says what they mean, and it is where the refusals are. Four different exception classes come out of this layer and which one a file gets is a property of the field that is wrong: Number=x throws java.lang.NumberFormatException because nothing wraps Integer.parseInt, Number=-1 throws TribbleException$InvalidHeader, Number=0 on a non-Flag type throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException from validate(), and Type=integer throws a plain TribbleException without the malformed-header prefix. Two of those are unchecked Java exceptions that no catch in the codec touches, so a malformed Number does not report a malformed header at all, and a port that funnelled every failure into one error type would answer a different question. Three asymmetries make the same line valid or invalid depending on context rather than on the line: INFO allows Type=Flag and FORMAT does not; a Flag with a non-zero count is silently rewritten to zero rather than refused, which is a value change and not an error; and Source and Version are read only from VCF 4.2, while under 4.1 they are not recommended tags either, so the tag-order check rejects the same line the 4.2 codec accepts. The rendered line is compared rather than the fields, because the rendering is what a writer emits and it carries the quoting rule as well as the values.

suites.title: Reading one VCF data line
suites.why: The vcf-record suite measures writing a record; this measures reading one, which is what GATK's VariantWalker needs and what nothing here has done before. Genotypes are excluded on purpose: htsjdk defers them through LazyGenotypesContext and the deferral is itself observable, so it is its own slice, and this stops at the eight site columns. Five behaviours decide what a record means and none is in the VCF specification. The splitter is not String.split: ParsingUtils.split fills a fixed-size array, steps over a delimiter at position zero instead of producing an empty first token, and condenses every trailing column into the last slot, so a line starting with a tab loses its first character and every genotype column after the first arrives joined back together in parts[8], which is why the column check compares against nine whatever the sample count. END overrides the stop and nothing validates it, so a record can end before it starts. A declared Flag written as KEY=0 is dropped from the attributes entirely rather than stored as false, and a bare key whose header type is not Flag becomes the string "." rather than a flag, so the header changes what a record contains. REF is upper-cased silently, so a lower-case REF is a rewrite and not an error. And an ALT of "." is checked and then not added, so the record carries one allele rather than two. The refusals are compared with their classes because parseQual throws a NumberFormatException that nothing catches while the neighbouring failures are TribbleExceptions carrying a line number. Attributes and filters are sorted in the dump: they live in a HashMap and a HashSet upstream, so their iteration order is not a property of the file and comparing it would compare the JDK.

suites.title: Reading the genotype columns
suites.why: The vcf-record-parse suite stops at the eight site columns; this is the rest, which htsjdk defers through LazyGenotypesContext until something asks for it. Four behaviours decide what a genotype contains and none is in the VCF specification. The GT separators are three characters, not two: VCFConstants.PHASING_TOKENS is a slash, a pipe and a backslash, and the split is a StringTokenizer, which drops empty tokens, so a backslash separates alleles like a slash does and 0//1, /0/1 and 0/1/ all yield the same two alleles as 0/1. A malformed AD or PL is silently dropped, because decodeInts catches NumberFormatException and returns null, which the builder stores as no-AD, while two lines further down the same method DP goes through a bare Integer.parseInt whose failure is not caught at all: the same malformed integer either disappears or aborts the record, decided by which key it was under. GT must be at position 0 when present and, before VCF 4.1, must be present at all, so the same record is valid or invalid depending on a header line. And a key with no value is skipped just as a value of "." is, but only the second had to be looked at, which shows in FT where "." means unfiltered rather than absent. GL is excluded: converting it to PL runs through GenotypeLikelihoods.fromGLField, which is floating-point work with its own rounding, and folding it in here would mix a numeric question into a parsing one.

suites.title: GL to PL, and the double parser under it
suites.why: A genotype carrying GL and no PL gets its PL computed here and every downstream tool reads the PL, so this is the last thing between a VCF with likelihoods in it and a port that can decode it. Three layers, and each has a decision a port gets wrong by default. Double.parseDouble is not Rust's f64 parser: Java accepts a trailing type suffix, hexadecimal floating point with a mandatory p exponent, leading and trailing whitespace up to and including the space character, and the spelled-out Infinity, while Rust accepts none of those and accepts inf and nan, which Java does not. VCFUtils.parseVcfDouble then catches the failure and retries against a case-insensitive infinity-or-NaN pattern, so inf and -INFINITY and nan parse after all, but only after the plain parse has failed. And GLsToPLs is one line with three decisions: the adjustment is the maximum of the likelihoods so the conversion re-normalises and the best genotype always comes out at zero whatever the input scale; MAX_PL is Integer.MAX_VALUE and the clamp is applied to the double before the rounding; and Math.round is floor of x plus a half, so it rounds half up rather than half away from zero, answers zero for a NaN, and returns a long that is then truncated to int. Reordering any of the three agrees on every ordinary genotype. The parsed doubles travel as raw bits, because a decimal rendering of a parse result hides exactly the disagreements this suite exists to find.

suites.title: AC, AF and AN
suites.why: GATK's ChromosomeCounts annotation is two lines that delegate straight to VariantContextUtils.calculateChromosomeCounts, so this is where the three commonest INFO fields in any VCF are decided, and four of its behaviours do not follow from the field names. AC and AF change type with the number of alternate alleles, one alt giving a scalar and two or more a list, so a consumer that fetched AC gets an Integer in one case and an ArrayList in the other even though both render the same way. A genotype whose FT is set contributes nothing and so does a no-call allele, for different reasons, which means AN is not the ploidy times the sample count. AF is not AC over AN: the numerator is the founders count for that allele and the denominator the founders total called count, while the AC reported alongside is the whole cohort's, so a port computing AF from the AC it has just written agrees on every unrelated cohort and disagrees on every pedigree. And the function removes keys as well as adding them, deleting AC and AF at a site with no alternate allele and all three where nobody is called, but only when removeStaleValues is on, which the annotation hard-codes to true. AF travels as raw bits because it is a division and a decimal rendering would hide a divergence in the last place.

suites.title: The genotype type ladder
suites.why: Genotype.determineType decides what every consumer downstream means by het and by called, and three of its answers contradict the javadoc above them. HET is two called alleles that are not equal, so C/G with no reference allele in it is HET, which is why isHetNonRef exists as a separate question and why a port defining HET as one ref and one alt disagrees on every multiallelic site. Equality is Allele.equals, which is bases and the reference flag, so a genotype holding the reference A and a non-reference A is HET while printing as A/A. And ploidy is not two: a haploid call is HOM_REF or HOM_VAR and never HET, a triploid A/A/C is HET, and MIXED is any genotype with at least one call and one no-call whatever its ploidy. VariantContext.isMonomorphicInSamples is measured alongside because it is the guard on GATK's SampleList annotation and it is not every genotype is hom-ref: a site carrying alternate alleles and no genotypes is not monomorphic, since the first disjunct needs no alternate allele and the second needs genotypes. The name order is measured because getGenotypesOrderedByName sorts with Collections.sort, which is String.compareTo, which is UTF-16 code units: uppercase before lowercase, 10 before 2, and a supplementary character BELOW U+FFFF because the first unit of its surrogate pair is 0xD83D, which is the opposite of code-point order and therefore the opposite of what Rust str comparison gives.

suites.title: FormatUtil number formatting
suites.why: 41,678 formatted doubles, and the corpus the README's 99.73% rests on. Its harness exists and its Rust test reads it, but no CI step has ever regenerated it against the oracle, so the rate is a property of the machine that produced the file rather than of the pinned reference. Decision 0011 makes this corpus locale-dependent, which is exactly the kind of thing the container pins and a developer machine does not.

suites.title: Percentile, Median and FastMath.round
suites.why: MathUtils.median in GATK goes through commons-math3 Percentile, which is Apache 2.0 and therefore transcribable where the JDK's own math is not (decision 0023). Four things here are not what the median suggests. The estimator interpolates, and its arithmetic is lower + dif * (upper - lower) rather than the mean of the two central values, which is a different double when they are far apart. The default NaN strategy is REMOVED, so a NaN shortens the array instead of ranking to an end, and an array of nothing but NaN answers NaN by way of an empty array. A single value is returned before the NaN strategy runs at all, so one NaN and two NaNs reach the same answer down different paths. And MathUtils.median finishes with FastMath.round, which is (long) floor(x + 0.5): the definition java.lang.Math.round stopped using in Java 7, so the two are one apart on 0.49999999999999994 and a port that reused the Math.round already in this crate would be wrong there. The jar is pinned to 3.5 because GATK's build.gradle declares strictly 3.5; the jmath corpus job downloads 3.6.1 for its FastMath columns, and that disagreement between two pins in this repository is open. Sixteen of its 312 percentile rows are an invalid operation's NaN, produced by the interpolation over infinities; x86-64 sets the sign bit and AArch64 does not, so the test exempts a NaN-sign-only difference off x86-64 and counts it, and asserts zero exemptions on the oracle's own architecture. That is decision 0012 reached by a second route.

suites.title: FastMath.exp, FastMath.log and their tables
suites.why: FastMath.exp is not java.lang.Math.exp. It is table-driven, pure Java and Apache 2.0, so unlike the HotSpot intrinsic withdrawn in decision 0014 it can be ported, and everything in commons-math3 that needs an exponential goes through it: Gamma, Erf, NormalDistribution, and therefore GATK's MannWhitneyU and every rank-sum annotation. The reference ships 6,175 lines of literal doubles for the four exponential tables and can also regenerate them with FastMathCalc, the choice being a compile-time constant set to the literals; the port was written on the computing branch and the oracle was asked whether the two branches agree. They do not: 577 of the 5,050 entries differ, all of them in the integer table, which is the only one built through splitReciprocal. That is decision 0024, and it means the port must carry the literals, since the literals are the branch that runs upstream. The golden carries both columns, read out of the same JVM, so the disagreement stays measured; 160 of the recomputed entries are an invalid operation's NaN, whose sign is the FPU's, which is decision 0012 arriving by a third route. The function itself is measured on the boundaries its own branches name: below -746 it underflows to zero, below -709 and at -709 it recurses on a shifted argument and divides by a magic constant so a subnormal result keeps its precision, and above 709 it overflows. The logarithm is here for the same reason and with the same two columns: eleven of the call sites in Gamma, Erf and NormalDistribution reach FastMath.log rather than Math.log, and the two differ in the last bit because only the JDK one is correctly rounded. Its table, LN_MANT, does agree with its recomputation, which places the disagreement of decision 0024 specifically on the reciprocal path rather than on FastMathCalc in general.

probes.title: Decision 0019: is re-sorting a sorted VCF header still a no-op?
probes.on_failure: Re-sorting is no longer stable. Decision 0019 needs revisiting.
probes.why: The port relies on it: writing a header that has already been through the comparator once must not reorder it. Measured stable, not proven stable, so it is re-measured.

probes.title: Decision 0016: is the VCF header comparator still inconsistent?
probes.on_failure: The comparator is now consistent. Decision 0016 can be revisited.
probes.why: The cycle is the reason the port uses a total order where htsjdk has none. If a future htsjdk made the comparator consistent, this fails and the divergence can be removed.

goldens_handled_elsewhere.why: Compared function by function against a corpus regenerated on real silicon, with per-function pass conditions from decision 0007, rather than by byte equality.
